translation_notes: translated.ldpy is byte-identical to original.py: the region constructs no RDF term at all. It parses a TriG document read from a file into a Dataset and asserts on a string. RDF only enters through ds.parse(data=..., format='trig') -- an opaque string handed to rdflib's parser -- and islands do NOT apply inside strings, so there is nothing for the notation to reach. This is the honest 'notation adds nothing' case, and it is a valid ldpy program unchanged

the mechanical draft had inserted five @prefix declarations in the middle of the parenthesised 'from nanopub import (' list (invalid ldpy); since not one prefixed name occurs in the region, they were all dropped
context shim: nanopub_shim.py puts the Nanopublication/nanopub-py@05022dc4bc checkout on sys.path (the package is not installed); one added import line, identical on both sides

data fixture: the pytest 'testsuite' fixture downloads github.com/Nanopublication/nanopub-testsuite at runtime; the driver replaces it with a stand-in exposing get_by_nanopub_uri only, backed by a local copy of invalid/plain/noprovlink.trig -- the entry the real connector's index returns for http://example.org/nanopub-validator-example/ (several suite files carry that URI; the index keeps the last one indexed, which is that file). MIT-licensed, 807 bytes, copied verbatim apart from a provenance header comment; read identically by both sides
driver: 'self' is unused by the region, so a None stand-in is passed; the region returns None, so the check rests on its own assert on np.metadata.np_uri
